results.input: Aria Voss needs to leave the Ice Citadel at once. Have her teleport out and describe how.
results.answer:
Aria cannot teleport out now. The Ice Citadel's four walls are warded and block teleportation [f34602a1]. Teleportation fails if any warded wall lies in the path [57e9dcc6], and only the Warden-General can lower a ward for one hour at a time [efeb2d52].

She has one exception: the Night of Thaw, the last night of the Long Winter, when the eastern wall unwarded for one hour (midnight to dawn) [c8557954]. If it is that night and she can reach the eastern side of the Citadel, she can teleport out—but she has only 20 mana and teleportation costs 50 [57e9dcc6], so she would need to restore her mana first.

Is it the Night of Thaw in your story? Or does she have another way to lower a ward?

The caster names a destination within one league (about five kilometres) and arrives there at once. A caster can carry only what they can carry on their own body. A teleporting caster cannot take another person with them.

Teleportation fails if the straight line to the destination crosses a warded wall, in either direction. A caster can teleport out of a warded place only if the path out does not cross a ward, which in practice almost never happens.

results.input: Sera Quill wants to open the Restricted Stacks of the Glass Library to read the blood-casting treatises. How can she get in?
results.answer:
Sera has a silver key already, so she can open the Restricted Stacks door immediately [d5a7cf5b]. No other access barrier is described for the door itself beyond the key requirement.

However, note that magic is silenced inside the Library except for spells cast by sworn Archivists [43a85e83]. If Sera tries to cast blood-casting spells from those treatises while inside the Library, they will fail and drain her mana.
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Sera Quill is at Glass Library, condition wounded, mana 75, health 60, carries: spellbook, silver key, ink vial

[search_lore] passage d5a7cf5b (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > The Restricted Stacks): The Restricted Stacks are a sealed wing of the Library where the most dangerous texts are kept, including the treatises on blood-casting. The door of the Restricted Stacks can be opened only with a silver key. There are exactly three silver keys. The Head Archivist holds one, the Deputy Archivist holds the second, and the Keeper of the Concord holds the third.
[search_lore] passage d9ce8de8 (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > The Library is warded): The Glass Library is warded on all sides. Teleportation cannot cross its walls, in either direction. Visitors arrive by the road, and the only way in is through the Door of Quiet on the southern side.
[search_lore] passage 43a85e83 (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > Magic inside the Library): All magic is silenced inside the Glass Library, except for spells cast by a sworn Archivist. The glass walls absorb every working of every discipline, so a visitor who tries to cast a spell inside the Library simply feels the mana drain away with no effect. A spellbook can be read inside the Library, but nothing can be cast from it.

results.input: Does Aria Voss have to strike her flint on steel before she casts fire magic in the Ice Citadel?
results.answer:
According to the lore, there is a conflict. The core magic rule says Aria does not have to strike her flint—possessing it is enough [d40003b6]. However, the Ice Citadel's Visitor's Primer says she must strike it on steel before every casting [8f22b8dd]. These two rules contradict each other, and nobody has tested which one actually applies.

Aria has flint in her inventory, so she can cast fire magic either way. But whether striking it is mandatory or optional depends on which rule is enforced—and your lore notes that it is currently unresolved.
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Aria Voss is at Ice Citadel, condition healthy, mana 20, health 85, carries: flint, broken sword, health potion

[search_lore] passage 8f22b8dd (The Ice Citadel > The Visitor's Primer): The Wardens give every visitor a short booklet called the Visitor's Primer. It lists the rules of the Citadel in plain words. It says that a visitor who wishes to cast fire magic must strike their flint on the steel before every casting, and that an unstruck flint is not enough.

This instruction does not agree with the law of magic recorded in the Archive of the Glass Library, which says that carrying the flint is enough. Visitors who have followed the Primer and struck their flint have never been refused, so nobody has tested which rule is right.
[search_lore] passage d40003b6 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Fire magic and the Ice Citadel): Fire magic cannot be cast inside the Ice Citadel unless the caster possesses flint. The walls of the Citadel are woven with the Frost Binding, an old working that smothers every spell of the Fire discipline the moment it is cast. Flint is the single exception, because a flint holds a stolen spark that the Frost Binding recognises and lets pass.

Possession means carrying the flint on one's person. It does not have to be struck, held in the hand or shown to anyone. A caster with a flint in a pocket can cast fire magic anywhere inside the Citadel.

The ban applies to magic only. Torches, candles, forge fires and the Great Hearth burn normally inside the Citadel, because ordinary fire is not a spell.

judge.reasoning: The answer correctly reports both rules: the core rule says possession is enough, and the Primer says the flint must be struck. It says the conflict is untested and unresolved, and it notes that Aria carries flint. One small issue: the answer attributes the possession rule to the core magic rule [d40003b6] rather than naming the Archive. results.input: Who can lower the wards of the Ice Citadel, and for how long?
results.answer:
Only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal of the Frost Wardens, and they can lower it for one hour at a time [f34602a1].

There is one exception: on the Night of Thaw, the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall's ward comes down automatically from midnight to dawn, allowing teleportation across that wall [c8557954].

[search_lore] passage f34602a1 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > How the wards work): The four walls of the Citadel are protected by wards that were raised after the founding of the fortress. They stop teleportation and scrying. Only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal of the Frost Wardens, and only for one hour at a time.
[search_lore] passage c8557954 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > The Night of Thaw): Once a year, on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall of the Citadel is unwarded. The ward on the eastern wall goes down at midnight and comes back up at dawn. The Wardens say that the ice must be allowed to breathe while the Frost Binding renews itself.

During the Night of Thaw the eastern wall can be crossed by teleportation like any open ground, and the guard on the Eastern Postern is doubled. The other three walls stay warded. The Frost Binding that smothers fire magic stays in force all night, so fire magic is still impossible inside the Citadel on the Night of Thaw unless the caster possesses flint.
[search_lore] passage 7df66575 (The Ice Citadel > Overview): The Ice Citadel stands on the Northern Reach, on a spur of black rock above a frozen sea. Its walls are cut from blue glacial ice and set on foundations of dark stone. About eight hundred people live there, most of them Frost Wardens, their families and the servants who keep the Citadel running. It is the seat of the Frost Wardens and the coldest inhabited place in Aethel.

The Citadel is reached by the Gate of Frost in the western wall. The winter lasts nine months, and the Long Winter, the hardest forty days of the year, closes every road to the Citadel except the Ash Road to the south, which is usually passable.

judge.reasoning: The answer says only the Warden-General can lower a ward, using the seal of the Frost Wardens, for one hour at a time. Passage f34602a1 supports all of this. It also says that on the Night of Thaw the eastern ward goes down from midnight to dawn and teleportation is allowed across that wall, which passage c8557954 supports. The word "automatically" slightly paraphrases the lore's "goes down", but this is a neutral wording detail and arguably implied. Both constraints are clearly satisfied.

constraints.constraint: Says only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal of the Frost Wardens
Says a ward can be lowered for only one hour at a time

results.input: Can Mira Sol cast fire magic while she is in Salt Harbour? Does she need flint?
results.answer:
Yes, Mira Sol can cast fire magic in Salt Harbour. Fire magic can be cast anywhere in Nox without any special object or restrictions except inside the Hollow Mine [1c9fa262]. Salt Harbour is not the Hollow Mine, so there is no ban.

She does not need flint. Flint has no meaning for magic in Nox [1c9fa262].
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Mira Sol is at Salt Harbour, condition wounded, mana 100, health 45, carries: star chart

[search_lore] passage 4add25e6 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour > The Tide Wards): The harbour walls are warded. The wards are called the Tide Wards, and they block teleportation in either direction. They are lowered for one hour at every full moon so that ships' crews can teleport their cargo ashore. During that hour a caster can teleport across the harbour walls for the normal price of 80 mana, without a Tide-key.
[search_lore] passage afb9b066 (Notable Characters of Nox > Mira Sol): Mira Sol is a navigator from Salt Harbour who learned to read the stars from her grandmother. She is a Tidemaster, with a mana pool of up to 300 mana, and one of the few in Nox who can teleport between ships at sea. She is bold, talkative and in debt.

Mira owes the Harbour Council the price of a lost Tide-key. She says that it was stolen, and the Council says that it was sold.
[search_lore] passage eb279661 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour): Salt Harbour is the great port of Nox, a city of white stone and tall masts on a bay of green water. About twelve thousand people live there. It is ruled by the Harbour Council, a body of nine ship-captains, and it is the only place in Nox where Tide-keys are issued.

[search_lore] passage 1c9fa262 (The Magic of Nox > Casting Rules > Fire magic): Fire magic can be cast anywhere in Nox without any special object, with one exception: it is forbidden inside the Hollow Mine, where the air holds firedamp that burns. Flint has no meaning for magic in Nox.
[search_lore] passage 8db439a2 (Places of Nox > The Hollow Mine > Fire in the Hollow Mine): Fire magic of any kind is forbidden inside the Hollow Mine, because the air holds firedamp. Open flames are forbidden too. Miners use sealed lanterns, which are lit with a spark from outside the mine. A caster who casts a fire spell inside the mine is expelled and fined.
